answer: kappa = 2^-182 is half of the smallest margin in the cost table. After dividing every cost by V = Tp, the seven dominant normalized costs are powers p^(1-g_i) of p. The smallest margin is g_2 = eps*c*(1-tau) = 2^-75 * 2^-56 * 2^-50 = 2^-181. It belongs to the chunk exchanges: their normalized cost p*K^(tau-1), with K = Theta(p^(eps*c)), is a power 1 - eps*c*(1-tau) of p. So every dominant term is at most p^(1-2kappa). The margin is taken to be 2kappa because one kappa pays for the fixed powers of log p (any fixed power of log p is at most p^kappa for large p) and the other kappa is the saving: p^(1-2kappa) * p^kappa = p^(1-kappa), and Tp * p^(1-kappa) = O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)). The fenilov page says that 2kappa may not exceed the smallest margin, so 2^-182 is the largest power of two that fits. The dedapov page says any kappa below 2^-181 would pass the same test, and I could not reconcile these two statements from the pages. The exponents eps = 2^-75, c = 2^-56 and 1-tau = 2^-50 are described as conservative fixed choices, and their product fixes the scale of kappa.

citations.quote: $\kappa=2^{-182}$, the exponent saved from the power of $\lg n$
Divided by $V=Tp$, the cost of each of seven kinds of operation is a power of $p$, and each of these exponents is at most $1-2\kappa$.
The smallest margin belongs to the chunk exchanges, whose normalized cost $pK^{\tau-1}$ is a power $1-\epsilon c(1-\tau)$ of $p$ because $K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$.
So the total is, up to a constant, $Tp\cdot p^{1-2\kappa}p^{\kappa}=Tp\cdot p^{1-\kappa}$, which is
one $\kappa$ of the margin absorbs the logarithmic factors and the other is the saving.
Hence $2\kappa$ may not exceed the smallest margin below one.
and $2^{-182}$ is the largest power of two allowed.
Half the smallest margin pays for logarithms and half remains as the saving.
Any positive $\kappa$ below $2^{-181}$ would pass the same test; $g_2$ sets the scale of $\kappa$.
The constants are conservative: no optimization is claimed.

stuck.quote: Any positive $\kappa$ below $2^{-181}$ would pass the same test; $g_2$ sets the scale of $\kappa$.
stuck.note: This page says any positive kappa below 2^-181 would pass. But the halving it describes requires 2kappa to stay within the margin, and the fenilov page says 2kappa may not exceed the smallest margin and that 2^-182 is the largest power of two allowed. I could not tell whether 2^-182 is forced by the argument or is a convention, and the two pages disagree.

stuck.quote: The constants are conservative: no optimization is claimed. They only need to give some fixed $\kappa>0$, and $\kappa$ is then forced by the cost accounting.
stuck.note: The page says kappa is forced by the cost accounting, but also that the constants are conservative and that none is optimized. I could not see what fixes kappa at exactly 2^-182 rather than some value below the margin, because the choices eps = 2^-75 and c = 2^-56 are not justified beyond being conservative.

stuck.quote: Half the smallest margin pays for logarithms and half remains as the saving.
stuck.note: I followed the arithmetic p^(1-2kappa) * p^kappa = p^(1-kappa), but not why the log allowance is kappa rather than some other amount, so the equal split is asserted, not derived.

stuck.quote: The product of three small exponents is unavoidably tiny
stuck.note: I could trace eps(2-tau) < 1-tau to the axis-layout margin g4 on the dedapov page, and tau(1+c/beta) < 1 to the layer conditions on this page. But the claim that the product is unavoidably tiny is not argued, and the page does not say why eps and c are these particular powers of two.

stuck.quote: for subspaces $E,E',G$ of tensor powers of $F$, $\dim(E\otimes G)=\dim E\cdot\dim G$
stuck.note: Tensor products are outside my background. I got past this by guessing that the dimension of a tensor product is the product of the dimensions, and then followed the dimension count without seeing the underlying construction.

stuck.quote: to save, the labels must confine all loss to one small edge.
stuck.note: I followed the sink-minus-source count that gives s = Wm - (N - 2L), but I could not see why the labels have to be chosen so that all loss falls on one small edge. The page states this as a requirement without a reason.

reason: Fairly sure of the arithmetic and of the structure. g_2 = 2^-75 * 2^-56 * 2^-50 = 2^-181, and kappa = 2^-182 is half of that; the table on the dedapov page and the explanation on the fenilov page agree on these numbers. The chunk-exchange margin in turn rests on tau = 1 - 2^-50, which the fizokid page says is chosen rather than derived. I checked its support against the dol page: the relative rank deficit of the bit network is about 1.5e-11, which exceeds 20*2^-50, so the stated condition holds. Less sure of why the margin is split in halves, and of why 2^-182 rather than a larger value below 2^-181: the fenilov page says 2kappa may not exceed the margin, while the dedapov page says any kappa below 2^-181 passes, and the pages do not settle this. I did not open the pages for the sifigeg, the power-saving recurrence, or the Sikited conjecture, since the question did not need them.
